title: Me levanto temprano
blurbEn: Ana's morning. This text introduces reflexive verbs — the ones where you do something to yourself — and how to say what time it happens.
body:
Me levanto a las siete. Es muy temprano.

Después me ducho.

Mi hermana se levanta más tarde. Ella nunca se levanta temprano.

A las ocho salgo de casa.
translationEn:
I get up at seven. It is very early.

Afterwards I shower.

My sister gets up later. She never gets up early.

At eight I leave the house.

me.note: 'Levantarse' means to raise yourself. The 'me' is doing the work of 'myself'.

las.note: Times are always feminine plural in Spanish: 'las siete', because it means 'the seven [hours]'.

phrases.note: Literally 'I raise myself'. The verb needs the 'me' — 'levanto' alone would mean lifting something else.
